# idkcraft — project review profile

## What this is
A hobby Minecraft stack: Paper server (`mc`), a Node 22 mineflayer bot (`bot/src`), and a CPU
"System-1" brain sidecar (`laya/shim.py`, FastAPI-shaped REST). Deployed by GitOps to Portainer.
The owner treats it as a learning project: changes should be readable and explain themselves.

## What a real failure looks like
- The bot crash-loops, disconnects, or stops ticking (`BRAIN_TICK_MS` loop stalls, unhandled
  promise rejection, mineflayer event never handled).
- The bot spams the remote brain when no player is online (cost guard in README is deliberate).
- A behaviour steals the tick from another one (follow stops while scouting, fight never yields).
- Secrets, hostnames, domains or IPs land in the repo (privacy rule in CLAUDE.md) — **critical**.
- A change to `docker-compose.yml` service names, env var names or the `laya` REST shape breaks the
  deployed stack (shared contract in CLAUDE.md, "do not rename").

## Blast radius
One private server, a handful of players. Wrong bot behaviour is annoying, not dangerous. A leaked
hostname or key is the one thing that cannot be taken back.

## Reporting bar
Report what breaks at runtime in the bot loop, in tests, or in the deploy contract. `npm test` in
`bot/` runs without a Minecraft client (fake-player harness) — a change that needs a live server to
be verified at all should say so, and a missing assertion for new branching logic is a finding.

## Deliberate conventions
- Ponytail rules: smallest diff, no speculative abstractions, one brain interface. A
  `// ponytail:` comment marks an intentional shortcut with its ceiling — not a finding.
- `ONLINE_MODE=false` + `ENFORCE_WHITELIST=TRUE`: intentional, the bot has no Microsoft account.
- Stub brain must keep working when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` / brain URL is absent.
- Plain CommonJS, no TypeScript, no framework beyond mineflayer + its plugins.

{"body":"Bead idkcraft-3nt.1: split the tick into perception + dispatch table + follow behaviour, with no behaviour change.

Why: index.js owned sensing, the brain-call dedup, and pathfinder goals in one closure, so follow/fight/scout work would collide on every PR. This cuts along sense / decide / act: perception builds facts, the ticker keeps the single brain call plus dedup, and each behaviour owns the pathfinder while chosen.

What changed (4 files, move not rewrite):
- bot/src/perception.js (new): HOSTILE_NAMES, findTarget(bot, followName), buildState(bot, target, lastTargetPos), stateKey — moved verbatim. buildState takes the previous target position and returns the next one on state._lastTargetPos; the ticker passes it through each tick.
- bot/src/behaviours/follow.js (new): the follow branch of applyDecision, exported as one function follow(bot, ctx, target). ctx is owned by the ticker ({ lastGoalKey, movements }). Keeps the re-issue-while-standing-still retry with its comment.
- bot/src/index.js (shrinks): keeps createTicker, cadence, dedup, log format, idle cost guards, and chat commands. The if/else on decision.action is now const BEHAVIOURS = { follow: ... } at module top; idle and unknown actions stop once. One commented every-tick seam sits right after buildState for the scout hook. No goal construction and no hostile list remain here.
- bot/test/tick.test.js: imports stateKey from perception; all existing assertions byte-unchanged; one new dispatch test (follow routes to the follow module with one setGoal, idle routes to one stop).

- bot npm test green, 20/20 (16 pre-existing assertions unchanged + new dispatch test).
- index.js has no GoalFollow and no hostile list (grep-checked; only behaviours/follow.js constructs the follow goal).
- Log line format and idle guards unchanged (no brain call without a player, slow poll when idle, one line per minute, dedup with stub-fallback retry).
- Live follow check not run locally (no game server running here; this is a pure move with identical logic). In-game follow/stop behaviour is unchanged by construction; please verify on the next playtest.

Seams for the next beads: fight adds one BEHAVIOURS entry on its own line; scout hooks the every-tick line. Both rebases should stay trivial.

Every env var the bot reads is still passed by compose; no new ones introduced.

Contract lens result on this change — clean:

- **Image build:** `bot/Dockerfile:5` is `COPY src/ ./src/`, a recursive copy, so the new `src/behaviours/follow.js` ships. Both new files are git-tracked at exact case (`bot/src/behaviours/follow.js`), which matters since the image runs on case-sensitive Alpine.
- **CI trigger:** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` tags the bot image by `git rev-parse HEAD:bot`; the `bot/` tree changed, so a new tag is built and pushed rather than reusing a stale one.
- **Dependencies:** the only new `require` is `mineflayer-pathfinder` in `behaviours/follow.js` — already a production dependency in `package.json` and present in `package-lock.json`, so `npm ci --omit=dev` still supplies it inside the image.
- **Env/service contract:** the bot reads `BRAIN_TICK_MS`, `MC_HOST`, `MC_PORT`, `BOT_USERNAME`, `BOT_FOLLOW` — unchanged from master and all passed by the `bot` service in `docker-compose.yml`. No service, port, volume or `laya` REST field touched (`brain.js` is not in the diff), so `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`-absent stub start is unaffected.
- **Privacy:** no hostname, domain, IP, key or token in any added line, nor in the PR #19 body or the commit message; `mc` and `laya` are compose service names, not hosts.
- **Export surface:** `stateKey` moved off `index.js`'s exports, but its only consumer was `tick.test.js`, updated in the same commit; `test/e2e-follow.js` imports nothing from `src/`.
